content:
Apple TV+ currently boasts a strong lineup of series, including popular titles such as "The Morning Show," "Ted Lasso," "Dark Matter," and the new Matthew McConaughey comedy "Brothers." But there's more good stuff coming. Below is everything premiering on Apple TV+ in October.

The Last First: Winter K2

  • Premiere date: October 2
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Documentary

Directed by Amir Bar-Lev, "The Last First: Winter K2" tells an intricate, thrilling yet deeply moving story that reveals the extreme mountaineering industry and its cultural evolution. The film focuses on a 2021 expedition aiming to become the first to summit K2 in winter — when conditions are at their most brutal — featuring climber John Snorri Sigurjónsson from Iceland and the Pakistani father-and-son duo Ali and Sajid Sadpara. On their perilous climb, they encounter a group of social media-driven climbers and their film crew, commercial expedition clients, and a team of Sherpas led by renowned Nepali mountaineer Nims. "The Last First: Winter K2" takes viewers up K2's frozen peaks, where unpredictable weather reveals a surprising, layered story — one of strategy and determination, class and caste, money and power — all unfolding in a life-or-death environment.

The Sisters Grimm (Season 2)

  • Premiere date: October 2
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Kids & Family

Two orphaned sisters live in a town full of fairy tale and fantasy characters, where they battle heroes and villains while investigating the mystery of their missing parents. "The Sisters Grimm" blends exploration, fantasy, and adventure into a tale with important lessons for viewers of all ages.

Small Prophets

  • Premiere date: October 7
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Comedy

"Small Prophets" tells the funny story of eccentric Michael Sleep (Pearce Quigley). Ever since his beloved Clea disappeared seven years ago, Michael has been living a mundane life — working at a hardware store, visiting his ageing father Brian (Sir Michael Palin), and hoping Clea will one day return. One day, Brian shares with him an ancient formula made from rainwater, horse manure, and a touch of alchemy. Sceptical but willing to try, Michael decides to create a "homunculus" — a magical spirit that can foresee the future — hoping to find the answer: will he ever see Clea again?

Matchbox The Movie

  • Premiere date: October 9
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Action

Based on the classic Mattel toy, "Matchbox The Movie" is an action-packed, globe-trotting adventure about a group of childhood friends who are thrust into a dangerous international chase when their former leader — undercover CIA agent Sean (John Cena) — resurfaces in their small town after years in hiding, forcing them to take on the mission of saving the world.

Tenzing

  • Premiere date: October 16
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Drama

Based on a true story, "Tenzing" tells the lesser-known tale of Tenzing Norgay (Genden Phuntsok). A gifted Himalayan mountaineer, he joined forces with New Zealand climber Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston) to become the first people to summit Mount Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (Thinley Lhamo) and supported by expedition secretary Jill Henderson (Caitríona Balfe), Tenzing convinced Colonel John Hunt (Willem Dafoe) to let him join the British expedition as a climbing member rather than a porter. Where Western climbers saw "Everest" as a peak to conquer, Tenzing revered "Chomolungma" as a sacred goddess of the mountains. The journey that followed was marked by tensions of background, class, and ambition — as well as the mountain's own deadly dangers. But at the top of the world, empire, class, and desire all fell away, leaving two outsiders bound by mutual respect and trust. For Tenzing, it was the fulfilment of a lifelong dream and a spiritual calling.

Where's Wanda? (Season 2)

  • Premiere date: October 21
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Dark Comedy

Apple's first German-language series, "Where's Wanda?" is a dark comedy about parents Dedo and Carlotta Klatt, who are desperate to find their 17-year-old daughter Wanda, missing for some time. With police making no headway, the family takes matters into their own hands — and, with the help of their tech-savvy son Ole, acquires surveillance equipment. Posing as utility company workers, they install bugs across the neighbourhood and half the suburb, only to discover that none of their neighbours are quite what they seem behind closed doors.

Nocturne

  • Premiere date: October 30
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Crime Drama

The series follows Jonah Lynn (Liev Schreiber), a jaded homicide detective on the streets of Philadelphia and a military veteran who decides to move to a small town in western Pennsylvania for a quieter life. But when the town and his family come under attack from cunning serial killer Jurek Walter (Graham), Jonah must protect everything he holds dear. With Jurek's last missing victim in danger, Jonah is forced to send his goddaughter, FBI agent Saga Bauer (Beetz), into a direct confrontation with Jurek. Just how far will Jonah go?

New episodes: "Slow Horses," "Brothers" and more

Several currently airing Apple TV+ series will also release new episodes in October, including:

  • "Ted Lasso": The Jason Sudeikis-starring comedy, airing through October 7
  • "Last Seen": A crime thriller, airing through October 7
  • "Slow Horses": The acclaimed British spy drama, airing through October 21
  • "Dark Matter": The sci-fi series starring Joel Edgerton, airing through October 30
  • "Brothers": The comedy starring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson, airing through November 4

Which of Apple TV+'s October offerings are you planning to watch? Let us know in the comments.

Apple TV+ costs $14.99 per month, with bundle discounts available through Apple One.
